newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends firmer, higher prices seen.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends firmer, higher prices seen.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures climbed to the day's high on late-session speculative short-covering, but the May contract failed to rally to its overhead target.
Still, today's close just below the high of 10.92 sets the stage for additional gains next week, market sources said.
May ended up 0.14 cent to 10.90 cents a lb, having ranged from 10.92 to 10.77. The back months settled 0.07 and 0.11 cent higher.
Volume was estimated at only 10,890 lots compared with Thursday's official 20,214 lots. Trade buying in the May/July spread and outright local buying in May was cited throughout the session.
"We've been down for a few days with plenty of opportunity to wash out the tremendous spec long position, but the short covering has been overwhelming," a broker said.
The failure of May to sink below support on Thursday sparked early gains. While several players had anticipated a run-up to 11.00 cents, scale-up trade selling provided firm resistance at the highs.

After attempting to overcome 10.89 cents several times during the session, the May contract slipped over the key level late in the day. The trade continued to provide resistance at each point higher and limited the rally at 10.92 cents.

Analysts said near-term resistance in May can be found at 11.00 cents and then at the recent high of 11.09 cents. Prices are expected to hold their current trading range amid a dearth of fundamental news.
Longer term, the May contract is seen falling to 10.50 cents on ample world supplies.
Players await the commitment of traders report released tonight.
